decisions.decision: Scope is everything: 13 plugins, 71 unique skills, 21 plugin agents, 4 canvases, 37 repo skills, 50 repo agents, 82 repo prompts, 1 hook, and 3 MCP servers
decisions.why: The reader should never have to leave the book to discover a tool, including the repo's own Spec Kit and WinUI assets
decisions.rejected: Plugins-only scope, which would hide the 37 repo skills and 50 repo agents that do most of the daily work

decisions.decision: Organization is dual: job-to-be-done category chapters plus a complete alphabetical index by source
decisions.why: Categorization is an editorial judgment that will not match every reader's mental model, so the source index guarantees nothing is unreachable
decisions.rejected: Category-only, which hides any entry whose category guess is wrong; source-only, which reproduces the original discovery problem

decisions.decision: Depth is deep for every entry: purpose, use cases, prerequisites, boundaries, and prompt examples
decisions.why: The audience is team onboarding, and a one-line listing leaves the reader exactly where they started
decisions.rejected: Quick-reference tables, which are cheaper to maintain but do not teach invocation

decisions.decision: Static HTML with a read-only drift-check script rather than a full generator
decisions.why: Editorial prose cannot be generated, but staleness can be detected, so the script reports missing, stale, and version-changed entries plus available updates without touching files
decisions.rejected: A full generator, which would produce accurate inventory and lifeless prose; no script at all, which lets the book rot silently

decisions.decision: Light editorial theme only, accent steel blue #1F4E79, with no dark mode
decisions.why: A single palette keeps print output correct by construction and removes an entire class of contrast bugs
decisions.rejected: A theme toggle, which would require print-specific overrides to remain correct

decisions.decision: All assets embedded locally with zero external network requests
decisions.why: The book must render offline and print reliably on a machine with no internet access
decisions.rejected: CDN-hosted fonts or stylesheets, which break offline and print unpredictably

decisions.decision: Print output is US Letter with a cover page, contents page, and one chapter per page break
decisions.why: The requirement is a physical book, so pagination is a first-class feature rather than a stylesheet afterthought
decisions.rejected: Screen-first layout with minimal print rules, which clips wide tables

decisions.decision: Duplicate skill names are documented once with all sources named
decisions.why: csharp-nunit ships in both csharp-dotnet-development and testing-automation, and double-counting would inflate the coverage claim to 72
decisions.rejected: Rendering two indistinguishable entries, which misleads the reader into thinking they differ

decisions.decision: Static HTML is the source of truth and the drift script parses the committed pages
decisions.why: The check then verifies what a reader actually receives rather than an intermediate model
decisions.rejected: A generator reading a JSON content model, which creates two sources of truth

decisions.decision: Twelve job-to-be-done chapters plus a complete source index
decisions.why: Plugin boundaries are invisible to a reader who does not already know the plugins
decisions.rejected: One chapter per plugin, which reproduces the discovery problem

decisions.decision: Fixed entry markup with data-entry-name/kind/source attributes
decisions.why: Exact, cheap drift detection immune to wording changes in visible text
decisions.rejected: Parsing headings, which needs fragile normalization

decisions.why: Supports search from any page over file:// without scanning every chapter
decisions.rejected: Fetching and parsing every chapter on load

decisions.decision: Dedicated print.html that inlines every chapter body
decisions.why: A multi-file series cannot produce one cover, one contents page, and continuous numbering
Keeps the series portable and offline instead of machine-specific

decisions.decision: Python 3 for check-drift.py with no third-party dependency
decisions.why: Python 3.14 is present, JSON handling is built in, and the script is platform-neutral
decisions.rejected: PowerShell, which is idiomatic here but more verbose for this parsing

decisions.decision: Duplicate skill csharp-nunit documented once naming both plugins, counted once
decisions.why: Inventory holds 72 directories and 71 unique names; overstating coverage would be dishonest
decisions.rejected: Two entries, which implies the skill differs by source

decisions.why: Prevents collisions such as winui-setup against winapp-setup and keeps deep links stable

decisions.decision: Coverage totals recomputed from committed HTML inside the drift script
decisions.why: 282 entries cannot be eyeballed, and an unverifiable number is a claim rather than a fact
decisions.rejected: Manual review against the inventory listing

concerns: At deep depth across 282 entries the series is likely 25-40 printed pages; category assignment becomes the main editorial risk
Four plugins ship only a canvas, so their chapters must document a surface rather than a skill list
The check script must stay strictly read-only and still report version deltas as actionable updates
At deep depth the series is 25-40 printed pages, so chapter assignment is the main editorial risk
Four plugins ship only a canvas, so those chapters document a surface rather than a skill list
Search ranked 18 of 20 sampled queries in the top three and 20 of 20 in the top five; the two misses sit at rank four and five inside a relevant answer set

step_summaries.summary: Plan fixes a twelve-chapter job-based taxonomy over a static HTML series with a read-only drift check
step_summaries.key_finding: The inventory holds 72 skill directories but only 71 unique skill names, so every count in the book must de-duplicate by name

step_summaries.summary: Built a 269-entry static HTML book with drift detection; all specified artifacts exist and verify
step_summaries.key_finding: The real fleet holds 269 unique entries, not the 282 estimated, because repo agents were overcounted and one skill is bundled by two plugins

approach: Static HTML authored per chapter against one stylesheet and one script, with a fixed entry markup contract so a read-only Python drift check can parse the shipped pages and compare them to live plugin and repo inventory.
